description: Avalanche Strikes Himlung Himal Base Camp In Nepal, At Least 10 Missing: how 10 outlets split  NewsCord
publisher.title: NewsCord
full_article:
Avalanche at Himlung Base Camp An avalanche struck the base camp of Himlung Himal, a 7,126-metre peak in Nepal’s Manang district near the Tibet border, and at least 10 people went missing on Sunday morning. Expedition organiser Mingma Gyalje Sherpa said, "The avalanche hit on Sunday morning," as expedition organisers reported that climbers and support staff were among those unaccounted for. Rishi Bhandari, general secretary of the Expedition Operators Association Nepal, confirmed the incident to The Kathmandu Post with "Yes, the incident is true," and he said two of those missing were associated with Imagine Nepal Pvt Ltd while eight were from Himalayan Holidays Nepal. “ ‘Yes, the incident is true,’ Bhandari told The Kathmandu Post. ” Deccan Chronicle Forecasts showed heavy snowfall around the 7,126m peak in recent days, and poor weather hampered rescue efforts as helicopters and rescue teams were unable to reach the site. The incident unfolded as Nepal was already dealing with severe weather, including heavy rainfall and snowfall that had forced climbers to retreat from autumn mountaineering expeditions. Left out by 9 of 10 who reported it Two bodies recovered . Reported by Hindustan Times. BBC Sources BBC Deccan Chronicle

Rescue Delays and Missing Helicopters and rescue teams remained unable to reach the Himlung Himal site because of adverse weather, and Bibhuti Chand Thakur of Himalaya Holidays Trekking told AFP that "Eight members of our expedition team and two more from another company have been reported missing." Mingma Gyalje Sherpa said the avalanche hit on Sunday morning, and he confirmed that two of his kitchen staff were among those missing. Rishi Bhandari said the missing included people linked to Imagine Nepal Pvt Ltd and Himalayan Holidays Nepal, while Ram Krishna Lamichhane, director general of Nepal’s Department of Tourism, said the department was closely monitoring the situation. The Department of Tourism urged trekkers and climbers to suspend activities as weather conditions deteriorated, and the Department of Tourism issued an alert advising that tourism activities be put on hold. The avalanche also came after Nepal’s adverse weather since Friday disrupted roads and prompted local authorities to close several sections to traffic. title: Dozens of Israelis receiving aid from insurance company after Nepal flooding - The Jerusalem Post
description: Dozens of Israelis receiving aid from insurance company after Nepal flooding  The Jerusalem Post
publisher.title: The Jerusalem Post
full_article:
Dozens of Israeli travelers in Nepal were receiving assistance on Sunday after heavy rain, flooding concerns, and severe weather disrupted major trekking regions across the country.

Clal Insurance & Finance said its rescue teams, operating through its partner firm, "Magen Search and Rescue," are on the ground rescuing Israeli travelers insured by the company who were caught in extreme weather in Nepal and needed help.

"Clal Insurance & Finance is working alongside all its rescue teams in Nepal to assist every policyholder in need of rescue. We are in contact with all relevant parties to ensure a safe outcome and to guarantee that all our policyholders are rescued and brought to safety," said Dror Zessler, deputy CEO and head of the Claims Division at Clal.

PassportCard said it was assisting 40 insured travelers in areas affected by the weather, including 17 in the Annapurna region, 17 in the Manaslu region, including Samagaon, four in the Tsum Valley near Chumling, and two in the Everest region.

Four of the travelers require medical attention and are expected to be evacuated for treatment once weather conditions permit, the company said. None of the insured travelers is currently believed to be in life-threatening danger, and their families are in regular contact with the situation room.

People carrying their belongings walk through Betrawati in Nuwakot district towards their village in Rasuwa, following deadly flash floods and a mudslide, in Nepal, September 21, 2026. (credit: REUTERS/Navesh Chitrakar)

Israelis trapped in Nepal say there is 'no way to go back'

Israelis talked to Israeli media about the situation on ground, with many trapped in certain areas that were closed down due to security risks. "There are landslides here every few hours on our heads. We don't have to wait for a disaster to happen," one Israeli woman told Ynet.

Yarin, an Israeli hiker who spoke with N12, said that there are "dozens of Israelis" trapped in the village of Samagaun, and there is no clear way to either go back or continue their trek due to the rains.

"Since last night, the weather conditions have been very difficult. There is no electricity, and there were rockfalls near us, and our lives were miraculously saved," Yarin added.

Local authorities issued warnings overnight due to the risk of flooding, and travelers staying at major tourist sites and along trekking routes were instructed to move to safer areas. Nepalese authorities had already warned trekkers to avoid high-altitude routes as heavy rain and snowfall threatened flooding, landslides, rockfalls, and damage to trails and bridges.

PassportCard teams were operating simultaneously in several locations and conducting ongoing assessments based on the weather and the ability to travel through affected areas. In the Annapurna region, insured travelers were staying in several villages while the situation room worked to help them continue their journeys when conditions allowed.

Nepal travel severely restricted as flood danger persists

Travel across large parts of Nepal remained severely restricted, with numerous roads blocked and trekking activities suspended in affected areas. Nepal's weather authorities had warned ahead of the storm that heavy rainfall could increase the danger of floods and landslides and urged travelers to suspend Himalayan treks.

According to PassportCard's current forecasts, the weather is expected to gradually weaken, although restoring normal travel in affected areas could take several days.

PassportCard said its situation room would remain available around the clock and continue assisting the travelers and their families until the emergency ends and normal travel can resume.

title: 10 Nepalese climbers missing after avalanche hits Himalayan base camp - Firstpost
description: 10 Nepalese climbers missing after avalanche hits Himalayan base camp  Firstpost
publisher.title: Firstpost
full_article:
At least 10 Nepalese climbers are missing after an avalanche struck a base camp near Himlung Himal in Nepal’s Manang district on Sunday morning, as heavy snowfall and poor weather hampered rescue efforts.

According to a BBC report, the climbers were part of teams preparing for expeditions on the 7,126-metre (23,380ft) Himlung Himal, located near Nepal’s border with Tibet.

They had been stationed at a staging point close to the mountain when the avalanche hit.

Eight members of one expedition team and two climbers working with another company have been reported missing, according to Bibhuti Chand Thakur of Himalaya Holidays Trekking.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Rescue efforts hit by bad weather

Rescue teams and helicopters have so far been unable to reach the site because of difficult weather conditions. Heavy snowfall has been reported around Himlung Himal in recent days, raising concerns about further avalanches and making access to the area difficult.

The missing Nepalese climbers had been sent ahead of foreign mountaineers to prepare the expedition camp, organise the route and fix ropes on the mountain.

Mountain districts across Nepal have experienced persistent rain and snowfall in recent days. The worsening conditions have created fresh risks for climbers and guides during the country's busy mountaineering season.

More from World

Earlier this week, climbers were forced to leave Mount Manaslu, the world's eighth-highest mountain, because of the growing threat of avalanches.

Purja among climbers killed in earlier avalanche

The latest incident comes less than two months after six climbers died in an avalanche on Broad Peak, including renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja.

Purja's body was recovered on August 2 at an altitude of around 5,700 metres. Three other bodies were also spotted on the mountain at the time, although their identities had not initially been confirmed.

The 43-year-old's death was announced by his expedition company, Elite Expeditions. Purja, who was born in Nepal and later served in the British Army, became widely known after climbing all 14 of the world's highest peaks in just over six months in 2019.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Extreme weather adds to Himalayan risks

The latest avalanche comes amid a series of weather-related disasters in the wider Himalayan region. Extreme weather in Uttar Pradesh has killed more than 20 people, officials said.

Meanwhile, recovery operations are continuing along the Nepal-Tibet border following a massive flood and landslide in August. More than 6,000 people are still reported missing, while more than 1,400 deaths have been confirmed after a glacial collapse sent large volumes of water and debris down the Trishuli River valley, sweeping through settlements.

At least 21 people have died, five are missing and five others have been injured across Nepal after four days of torrential rain triggered floods and landslides in several parts of the country, authorities said on Sunday. The severe weather from September 24 to 27 also forced the evacuation of around 3,000 people and damaged or destroyed hundreds of homes.The latest warning came after the Narayani River in central Nepal crossed the danger level of nine metres on Sunday morning and entered settlements. Several highways leading to Chitwan, a key road junction connecting different parts of the country, also remained blocked by landslides.Authorities warned residents in low-lying areas to remain alert as the continuing rain increased the risk of further flooding and landslides.According to an update from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), landslides accounted for 14 of the deaths. Five people remain missing in landslide-related incidents.Floods have killed four people, while three others died following continuous heavy rainfall.A separate landslide in Nishikhola Village Council of Baglung district killed four people on Sunday morning, local authorities said.“In Nishikhola Village Council of Baglung District, four people have died after being buried in a landslide. The incident occurred this morning in Ward Number 3, Hardra,” Prem Bahadur Gharti Magar, the deputy chairperson of the village council, told ANI over the phone.The Kaligandaki River in Baglung has also swept away houses and bridges, cutting off road connectivity in parts of the district.NDRRMA earlier issued a high-alert advisory for people living along major river basins after landslides blocked or partly obstructed river flows.A landslide in Chame, the headquarters of Manang district, obstructed the flow of the Marsyangdi River. Another landslide in Nisi, Ward 3 of Thasang Rural Municipality in Mustang, partially blocked the Kali Gandaki River.The authority urged people living downstream to remain extremely cautious because of the risk of sudden water releases if the blockages give way.Landslides at several locations have also hampered search and rescue operations, while conditions continued to deteriorate because of the persistent rain.The severe weather has directly affected 247 families across Nepal. NDRRMA said 260 homes were completely destroyed and another 80 suffered partial damage.Emergency teams have moved around 3,000 people from high-risk areas to safer locations. Armed Police Force personnel and local authorities have been involved in rescue and relief operations, including providing food and other essentials to displaced families.In the worst-hit mountain districts of Jajarkot, Myagdi and Sankhuwasabha, helicopters were used to evacuate people who were trapped.NDRRMA Spokesperson Shanti Basnet said district administration offices in all 77 districts, along with all three national security agencies, remained on high alert as authorities continued collecting data and carrying out recovery work.The downpour was triggered by a low-pressure system originating in the Bay of Bengal, NDRRMA said.Its monitoring stations recorded more than 100 mm of rainfall at 106 locations during the four-day period.Dumkuali in Nawalparasi (Bardaghat Susta East) recorded the highest rainfall at 455.2 mm. Pokhara in Kaski received 407.2 mm, while Anbu Khaireni in Tanahun recorded 373.2 mm.As the storms intensified, NDRRMA's Central Monsoon Response Command Centre directed local authorities to stop vehicle movement on vulnerable road sections. Schools were also closed in affected districts.The agency sent more than 5,000 direct SMS alerts to field responders. The Flood Forecasting Division sent more than 814,000 early-warning messages to people living in downstream flood-risk areas.The bad weather has also raised concerns for thousands of foreign tourists and trekkers in Nepal.NDRRMA estimated that around 9,000 foreign tourists and trekkers were in the country during the period of heavy rain. In coordination with the Nepal Tourism Board and local trekking agencies, the authority issued safety advisories in English.Tourists in vulnerable terrain were urged to take shelter and suspend travel until conditions improved.Two bodies recovered after Himlung Himal avalancheNepal is also dealing with a separate disaster in the high-altitude Manang district.Two bodies were recovered after an avalanche at the base camp of Himlung Himal, according to NDRRMA and Nepal Police.The mountain region had experienced heavy snowfall for several days, forcing climbers to retreat from autumn expeditions. Others remained missing after Sunday's avalanche.At 7,126 metres, Himlung Himal is one of Nepal's high-altitude climbing destinations. Helicopter flights to the area require an additional permit, making rescue operations more difficult.The latest floods and landslides come about a month after the devastating Bhotekoshi floods, which have so far claimed more than 1,400 lives and left over 6,000 people missing, according to the information provided by authorities.The August 26 disaster began in riverside settlements in Rasuwa district before rapidly affecting neighbouring Nuwakot and Dhading.The floods caused extensive infrastructure damage. Eight operating hydropower projects with a combined capacity of 281 MW and four projects under construction with a combined capacity of 388 MW were damaged.Major sections of the Galchhi-Betrawati-Rasuwagadhi road and the Prithvi Highway were also destroyed or badly damaged. The disaster affected 48 suspension bridges and 31 motorable bridges.Earlier, Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah used his UN General Assembly address to highlight the growing risks facing the Himalayan region.He thanked India and China for their “prompt and generous assistance” following the August disaster.Shah said warming was destabilising the fragile Himalayan ecology by thawing permafrost and weakening mountain slopes. He said this was increasing the risks of ice-rock avalanches, floods, landslides and other cascading hazards.

title: Avalanche at Himlung Himal in Nepal leaves 2 dead, 14 missing - dw.com
description: Avalanche at Himlung Himal in Nepal leaves 2 dead, 14 missing  dw.com
publisher.title: dw.com
full_article:
Two people have died when an avalanche struck the base camp of a mountain in Nepal with at least 14 others still missing.

The avalanche hit the 7,126-meter (23,380-foot) Himlung Himal after several days of heavy rain and snowfall across the region.

The dead and missing are all mountain guides and staff of Nepalese expedition companies who had been preparing the base camp for paying customers to climb the mountain.

"There were a total of 14 kitchen staff members and two climbing guides from different companies who were missing," the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association said. "The two climbing guides have been found, but sadly, both were found deceased."

Unclear how many are missing

There was conflicting information as to how many people were in the affected area near the border with Tibet at the time of disaster. Local police said there were at least 22 people at the base camp when the avalanche struck on Sunday morning.

Bibhuti Chand Thakur, head of trekking company Himalayan Holidays Nepal, told news agency DPA that search and rescue operations were under way. "The chance of survival remains high because of fresh snow," he said, adding that he did not yet have a definitive number of missing or survivors, as the area is remote and cut off from communication.

While Mount Everest (pictured) is Nepal's most famous peak, peaks like Himlung Himal are also popular with climbers [FILE: May 21, 2024] Image: Narendra Shahi Thakuri/dpa/picture alliance

Authorities had warned of severe weather across Nepal over the weekend. Rain has affected much of the country since Thursday, with snowfall reported in the higher northern regions. The conditions have disrupted roads and trekking routes and led authorities to suspend climbing and trekking activities on several mountains.

The Himalayan nation is home to eight of the world's 14 mountains higher than 8,000 meters, and trekking and mountaineering tourism is vital to the country's economy.

The latest avalanche comes as Nepal continues to recover from devastating floods in August that killed more than 1,400 people and left thousands missing.

Edited by: Wesley Dockery

Sixteen expedition support staff are feared dead after an avalanche buried tents at Himlung Himal (7,126m) base camp in Nepal’s Manang district under more than 15ft of snow on Sunday morning. Rescuers recovered two bodies while 14 others, mostly kitchen staff, remained missing. Search teams said chances of finding survivors were slim. Operations were suspended later in the day due to difficult conditions and were scheduled to resume Monday morning.Members of the search and rescue team identified the two deceased as climbing guides Pasang Bhote and Chhebi Bhote. “We will resume the search for the 14 other kitchen staff,” Mingma G Sherpa, who led the rescue operation, told TOI. The avalanche struck while a Himalayan Holidays Nepal team was preparing the base camp for a 14-member all-women group from a climbing school in the UAE, scheduled to arrive in Kathmandu on Oct 1.Himlung Himal, in the Nar Phu region of Manang, had witnessed persistent rain and heavy snowfall before the avalanche. At least eight IFMGA/NNMGA guides were mobilised for the rescue, but poor weather restricted access to the base camp.“It is very unlikely that the missing people will be found alive, as the tents were buried beneath more than 15ft of snow,” rescuers involved in recovering the bodies said.Nepal's department of tourism said 14 staff from Himalayan Holidays and two kitchen workers from Imagine Nepal Treks were caught in the avalanche. Initial reports had put the number of missing people lower before expedition organisers and authorities revised the figure after receiving details from the remote site.The accident came amid a deadly 2026 climbing season across Himalayas and Karakoram, where at least 24 climbers and high-altitude workers had already died before Sunday’s incident. The toll included fatalities during Nepal’s spring season, an avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakista-occupied Kashmir n and four deaths on Manaslu this month.

title: 2 Killed, 10 Missing After Avalanche Strikes Nepal's Himlung Himal Peak - NDTV
description: 2 Killed, 10 Missing After Avalanche Strikes Nepal's Himlung Himal Peak  NDTV
publisher.title: NDTV
full_article:
Two people were killed and 10 others remained missing after an avalanche struck the Himlung Himal peak in Nepal's Manang district on Sunday, police said.

The avalanche at the base camp of the 7,126 metre Himlung Himal peak in the Nar Phu area buried a tent where nine climbers and 13 support staff were taking shelter.

Around 12 people went missing after the incident, according to Deputy Superintendent of Police Shailendra Thapa.

Bodies of two people were found on the peak later, while 10 others remained missing, police said.

According to Thapa, all those missing are Nepalese nationals.

A helicopter was dispatched to the incident site for a rescue operation, he said.

The missing belong to Himalayan Holidays Nepal (HHN) and Imagine Nepal Treks, who lost contact with their people after the avalanche struck, according to an official at HHN.

"One of the expedition members telephoned and informed that their friends have gone missing after the avalanche hit the base camp," the official said.

According to the official, the expedition member said they were scattered after the incident and there is no information about others.

Several missing after avalanche hits Himlung base camp in Nepal. -File photo: IANS

Kathmandu, Sep 27 (IANS) Several Nepali expedition guides and support staff are missing following an avalanche that hit the base camp of Mt. Himlung in Nepal’s Manang district on Sunday, concerned expedition companies said.

They were at the base camp to fix ropes and set up tents ahead of the autumn climbing season.

“We have been informed that more than half a dozen of our staff are missing following the avalanche, but we cannot confirm the figure as contact could not be established after we briefly spoke with one of our staff early Sunday morning,” said Barun Bhandari, general manager of an expedition company.

He said more than 20 staff members from his company were part of the team at the base camp.

Likewise, another expedition company, also confirmed that some of its staff were affected by the avalanche but did not confirm the number.

The Kathmandu Post reported that at least 14 Nepalis are missing on Himlung Himal in Manang’s Nar Phu region following the avalanche, citing trekking officials.

Chief District Officer of Manang district Mukti Prasad Khanal said the number of missing people could not yet be confirmed.

“Rescue helicopters have been sent to the area where the avalanche occurred,” he said.

The incident comes just a month after a catastrophic flooding disaster near the Nepal-China border, triggered by a huge glacier collapse and landslide, killed more than 1,400 people and left more than 5,000 missing.

Tourism is one of Nepal’s key sources of income, and following the Bhotekoshi flooding disaster, the country has been urging tourists to visit Nepal, saying that other parts of the country remain safe.

Earlier, the District Administration Office, Manang, had prohibited trekking in several high-altitude areas from September 25 to 27 following forecasts of heavy to very heavy rainfall and snowfall in the higher Himalayan areas.

It said the restriction was imposed following a decision by the District Security Committee in view of the potential risk of loss of life due to the adverse weather conditions.

Nepal has been experiencing incessant rainfall in several parts of the country since September 24, with water levels in several rivers rising significantly, prompting authorities to advise people living along river corridors to move to higher ground.

The avalanche hit Mount Himlung, a 7,126-meter (23,380-foot) peak in north central Nepal, said Mukti Prasad Khanal, the chief government administrator of Manang District where the mountain is located.

All those killed or missing were Nepali nationals.

Rescuers brought two bodies and 10 survivors down from the mountain by helicopter to a nearby town, Khanal said.

The search was expected to resume at first light Monday, he said.

Authorities had warned of severe weather across the Himalayan nation over the weekend. It has rained across Nepal since Thursday, with snowfall in the northern mountain regions.

Nepal is recovering from devastating flooding in August that swept several villages, leaving more than 1,400 people dead and nearly 6,000 others missing.
